parts.text: A student investigates the resistance of a wire. Fig. 3.1 shows the circuit he uses. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student measures the current and decides that he wants to use a lower current. He adds a variable resistor to the circuit to reduce the current. On Fig. 3.1, mark with an X a suitable position in the circuit for the variable resistor. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text: a position in series with power supply, ammeter and BC

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student measures the current I in the circuit. I = ......................................................... [1] Fig. 3.2 Fig. 3.3

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student places the sliding contact at a distance l = 85.0 cm from B . He measures, and records in Table 3.1, the potential difference (p.d.) V across the length l of resistance wire BC . Record, in Table 3.1, the potential difference shown in Fig. 3.3. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student repeats the procedure using l values of 65.0 cm, 45.0 cm, 25.0 cm and 5.0 cm. His readings are shown in Table 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the resistance R of 85.0 cm of the resistance wire using the equation R = V I . [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Complete the column headings in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 l / cm V / R / 5.0 0.2 0.53 25.0 0.8 2.11 45.0 1.4 3.68 65.0 2.0 5.26 85.0 [1]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Plot a graph of resistance R ( y ‑axis) against length l ( x ‑axis). Start both axes at the origin (0,0). 0 0 [4]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
graph:
axes correctly labelled with quantity and unit and right way round
suitable scales
all plots correct to ½ small square

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Use your graph to determine the resistance R 50 of 50.0 cm of the resistance wire. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. R 50 = ............................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text:
method shown clearly on graph
R value correct to nearest ½ small square
